scripts.//test: Runs the unit suites AND every behavioural matrix, unconditionally. This used to be `pnpm -r test && pnpm test:rls`, where one unit failure anywhere short-circuited the only tests that assert tenant isolation, and nothing recorded that they had been skipped. The matrices are now DISCOVERED from supabase/tests/*.test.mjs, so one that is added and never wired up cannot exist, and a matrix that reports no RESULT line fails the build (audit 2026-08-09).
scripts.//test:rls: The behavioural matrices alone. History worth keeping: two of them (load-lifecycle, duty-sessions) were never wired in and had not executed in months behind stale migration filenames, while the ledger quoted their pass counts — 42/42 and 20/20 — as fact. Both counts turned out to be real, but only after four unimplemented behaviours the matrices specified were actually built (migrations 0141-0143). They were also chained with `&&`, so the first failure hid the other three.
scripts.//verify:live: Answers "why don't I see my changes?" in one command: compares git HEAD + the highest migration file against the deployed API's GET /api/version. Exits non-zero on drift.
scripts.//gen:tokens: Regenerates packages/ui/src/tokens.generated.css from the DTCG sources in packages/tokens/src. The @theme inline block is DERIVED from each token's `silvicom.expose` extension, so a role can no longer arrive without its Tailwind binding — the border-line failure mode, closed at the source rather than linted for.
scripts.lint:migrations: node scripts/check-migration-versions.mjs && node scripts/check-driver-references.mjs && node scripts/check-driver-references.mjs --self-test
scripts.//lint:migration-ordering: A merged commit is SERVED about nine minutes before its migration is APPLIED — Railway deploys on push, migrate.yml waits for CI green. So a column and its first reader must ship in two different merges, or the app spends that window asking PostgREST for something the database does not have. Measured on #430 (2026-09-01): the inspections page returned 500 for 9m10s. New TABLES are exempt — their readers are new code paths, so the window degrades a feature nobody is using yet rather than breaking one they are.
scripts.//lint:driver-references: Every drivers(id) FK is accounted for by the merge (D-SEP5, SEPARATION-PROGRAM-PLAN P2.5). merge_driver was re-issued eight times because nothing connected a new driver FK to the merge; found FIVE unhandled FKs on its first run — one of which (financial_entries, on delete restrict) made merges abort outright. The mechanical moves live in modules/roster/mergeDriver.ts and ride into merge_driver_v2 as a validated parameter; a new FK is one TypeScript line, enforced here. Chained onto lint:migrations.
scripts.//check:card-binding: Phase 2's exit gate, scripted (Step 2.6): no org may hold write_entitlement = 'confirmed' with a null probed_identity_hash. Deliberately NOT in ci.yml — it reads the live database, and this repository is public, so wiring it there would mean a production service-role key in CI secrets to check a status claim. Run it at session start and after any probe or credential change; migration 0194 enforces the same rule in Postgres.
scripts.lint:rls: node scripts/check-rls.mjs && node scripts/check-section-policies.mjs && node scripts/check-section-policies.mjs --self-test
scripts.//lint:section-policies: The SECTION_ACCESS matrix and the SQL mirroring it cannot drift silently (D-SEP10, SEPARATION-PROGRAM-PLAN). Any auth_role() role list in a migration above 0260 must equal rolesThatManage/rolesThatCanView for the table's section (module from table-modules.json, section from the gate's MODULE_SECTIONS map) or carry a section-policy-waiver line — so the accounting/billing/maintenance sections are born checked. History grandfathered by the boundary; the route-mount half of D-SEP10 lands at P4.2 as a runtime routeAuth.test extension instead of a regex that would lie. Chained onto lint:rls so CI runs it without a workflow edit.
scripts.//lint:rpc-org-default: An org-scoped RPC must be callable BY A BROWSER. D-FC1 is `security invoker` + `coalesce(p_org, auth_org_id())`, and three functions implemented the coalesce while declaring `p_org` first with no DEFAULT — so PostgREST, which resolves on the named arguments supplied, could find no form that omits it. `/ifta` and the Buy discipline tab were dead on arrival and every test passed, because a test calls the function WITH an org and a positional `(…, null)` resolves fine without a default. Only the browser omits the argument (0258).
scripts.//lint:capabilities: Fails when a capability decision this codebase paid for comes undone (R9; D-ROS2/D-ROS7/D-ROS11): `canManageFleet` used as an identifier anywhere in apps/web — one boolean standing in for an 11-section × 8-role matrix, and every workaround the roster plan removed was downstream of it; a `requiresManage` route meta that does not NAME a section; or a surface that edits driver fields without building them from `DRIVER_INLINE_EDITABLE`, which is how a field acquires a second editor with a different amount of honesty. It PARSES rather than greps: R0's value was writing down why the boolean died, and three files explain it by name — a gate that forbade saying it would delete the reasoning it protects. `--self-test` proves all three detectors fire and that none fires on a comment.
scripts.//lint:upserts: Bans `.upsert(x, { onConflict: "id" })` into a table with NOT NULL columns the payload cannot be shown to carry. Postgres evaluates NOT NULL on the proposed tuple BEFORE conflict arbitration, so that call fails on rows that already exist — the defect that shipped three times and took the Idling and HOS syncs down (incident 2026-08-10).
scripts.//lint:tests: Fails when a *.test.* file exists that its workspace runner never collects. Third occurrence of that bug: apps/driver narrowed `include` to tests/** and 24 cases in src/ had never run (audit 2026-08-09).
scripts.//mutation:check: Breaks the code on purpose and requires the suite to go red. A SURVIVED mutation is a hole in the tests; a STALE one means the code moved and that check has been testing nothing. Runs weekly in CI (.github/workflows/mutation-check.yml).
scripts.//lint:secrets: gitleaks over `git archive HEAD` — tracked content only, so an untracked local .env never false-alarms while a committed one fails the build. Needs the gitleaks binary (brew install gitleaks).
scripts.lint:boundaries: node scripts/check-feature-boundaries.mjs && node scripts/check-feature-catalog-parity.mjs && node scripts/check-table-access.mjs && node scripts/check-table-access.mjs --self-test && node scripts/check-shared-contracts.mjs && node scripts/check-shared-contracts.mjs --self-test
scripts.//lint:shared-contracts: One contract, one home (P6.2, SEPARATION-PROGRAM-PLAN — the last hand-held ARCHITECTURE §6 rule becomes a gate; hit twice by its own author during P6.1). A contract-shaped app export may not shadow a shared export or appear in two apps; vendor parser functions in shared may never be value-imported by a browser app (D-SEP11 converse) except by pinned argument. Chained onto lint:boundaries so CI runs it without a workflow edit.
scripts.//lint:table-access: Raw collected data is readable only by its owning collector (D-SEP1, SEPARATION-PROGRAM-PLAN). check-feature-boundaries scans imports, so all 39 staging reads the 2026-08-27 audit found passed a green build; this gate scans actual table access — .from() literals across api/web/admin-api/driver, dynamic .from(<expr>) indirection (error unless pinned), and raw-table references in new migration SQL (raw-access-waiver line required). 35 measured sites grandfathered, shrink-only. Chained onto lint:boundaries so CI runs it without a workflow edit.
scripts.//lint:table-producers: No table ships without a producer. Four tables merged 2026-08-24 with zero application code (financial_entries + three mcleod_* staging), terminals sat dead since 0097 with three roster FKs pointing at it. A table is written somewhere — .from() in app code or DML in an RPC body — or it carries a pinned waiver naming the plan that owes the producer (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6, D-ARC3).
scripts.//lint:table-writers: No table quietly gains a new writer. fuel_transactions reached 35 writing files and CDL expiry lived in two unsynced places before anyone was asked to justify a write site. Every (table ← file) write pair is pinned in scripts/table-writers.json; a new one fails the build until it is added deliberately in the same PR — and stale pairs must be removed, so the manifest only tightens toward the D-ARC3 ownership map.
scripts.lint:table-writers: node scripts/check-table-writers.mjs && node scripts/check-table-modules.mjs && node scripts/check-table-modules.mjs --self-test && node scripts/gen-schema-snapshot.mjs && git diff --exit-code -- supabase/schema.generated.sql
scripts.//lint:schema-snapshot: supabase/schema.generated.sql is the applied-state rendering of migrations/ (D-SEP2, P2.6) — regenerated by gen-schema-snapshot.mjs from the same PGlite the matrices use, sorted for stable diffs, so a migration PR shows its net schema effect in one hunk. The diff check fails on hand edits or a forgotten regenerate (the lint:codegen convention). Chained onto lint:table-writers so CI runs it without a workflow edit.
scripts.//lint:table-modules: Every table has exactly one owning module and a declared layer (D-SEP2, SEPARATION-PROGRAM-PLAN). scripts/table-modules.json is the machine-read ownership record; the gate holds it complete against live migrations, holds every pinned write site inside its owner's directory (70 measured 2026-08-27 sites grandfathered, ratchet-only), and fails any migration above 0260 that touches two modules' tables without a cross-module-waiver line. Chained onto lint:table-writers so CI runs it without a workflow edit; --self-test proves all three detectors can fire.
scripts.//lint:template-integrity: Three ways a Vue template can be wrong that nothing else checks, each of which had SHIPPED (HazmatGuard audit 2026-08-30, docs/plans/hazmat-consolidation/): a PascalCase tag used and never imported, which Vue renders as an unstyled unknown element and vue-tsc does not resolve — HazmatProductLines shipped <BaseCard> unimported, so the public placard calculator's main card was never a card; Tailwind !important on a shared primitive, which apps/web/CLAUDE.md forbids and which always means a variant is missing; and an <a href="/api/…">, which cannot authenticate because the API takes only a bearer header, so HazmatPanel's packet link 401d for everyone. Deliberately NOT a capitalize-on-badge rule: badges.ts sanctions that for unmapped vocabularies and eleven sites legitimately use it, so it is pinned by a test instead. Chained onto lint:ui-adoption so CI runs it without a workflow edit.
scripts.//lint:cli-streams: efs.mjs must put ONLY a JSON result on stdout — a prompt there makes `efs.mjs <cmd> > file.json` hang, which it did on 2026-08-16.
scripts.//lint:agent-syntax: Every tools/** module must PARSE. eslint.config.js excludes tools/** on purpose (the on-prem agent runs on the carrier's Node, not the app's), which left it with no gate at all — on 2026-08-28 a backtick inside a SQL comment terminated the template literal it lived in and the agent died at IMPORT, stopping every McLeod sweep at once while CI stayed green. Chained onto lint:cli-streams so CI runs it without a workflow edit.
scripts.//mcleod:inspect: Read-only reconnaissance against the carrier's LoadMaster: the 22 aggregate questions the field mapping cannot answer without measuring. Posts nothing to FuelGuard and needs no ingest token — the people best placed to run it are the carrier's IT against `lme`, before any token exists. Every query is gated by lint:mcleod-recon.
scripts.//mcleod:dry-run: Reads McLeod, maps every row, and prints per-field coverage plus one sample — without posting and without a FuelGuard ingest token. Exercises the whole carrier-side half of the integration (the SQL, the trims, the date and code handling, the change detection) against real data before the two systems are connected at all. Driver names, licences, addresses and dates of birth are masked: coverage counts prove the mapping, printing the values proves nothing extra.
scripts.//mcleod:report: The match report computed BY the pipeline, writing nothing — not a row, not even last_synced_at. This is what M3's Done-when actually asks for and the go/no-go for everything after it: its counts must reproduce the plan's hand-computed 162 / 175 / 201.
scripts.//lint:mcleod-recon: The McLeod recon pack (tools/mcleod-agent/inspect.mjs) is meant to be run by the CARRIER'S IT against `lme`, the production LoadMaster database our login cannot read (HAS_DBACCESS = 0). Its reviewer has to be able to trust 22 SQL statements without reading them closely, so the gate enforces the four properties that make it safe to hand over: every statement is a single SELECT; the outright-banned columns (social_security_no and friends — db_datareader can read it and 1,461 of 1,463 rows have one) appear nowhere at all; names, licences, addresses and contacts may be COUNTED but never returned; and anything reading driver/tractor/trailer binds @companyId, because dbo.company holds four legal entities in the same tables.
scripts.lint:codegen: node scripts/gen-rule-catalog.mjs && pnpm gen:tokens && git diff --exit-code -- 'packages/**/*.generated.ts' 'packages/ui/src/tokens.generated.css'
scripts.//lint:token-schema: The 14 role names apps/web and apps/driver genuinely share — canvas, surfaces, ink, edges. Measured 2026-08-23: of 61 web roles and 33 driver roles only those 14 overlap, so the gate pins the shared neutral ground rather than pretending the two schemas match. Everything else is the two products being different (operation-*/sync-* on driver, elevation-*/viz-*/link on web).
scripts.//lint:light-dark: Lightning CSS transpiles light-dark() into a prefers-color-scheme polyfill by default, which follows the OS and cannot be overridden by the in-app scheme toggle. Both vite configs must exclude Features.LightDark. The toggle shipped broken because every other gate reads source CSS and the rewrite happens at minification (2026-08-23).
scripts.//lint:token-gamut: Every colour token must name a colour an sRGB display can actually produce. 64 of 264 did not (2026-08-25) — ramp-caution-200 was 0.212 of linear overshoot, outside Display-P3 too. Chrome keeps oklch() all the way to PAINT rather than resolving it to rgb(), so an out-of-gamut token is mapped against the display profile: macOS colour-manages and can paint into P3, Windows does not, and the same dashboard came out visibly different on two machines driving the same monitor.
